Product Design audit · 14 November 2026

Make the adaptive observation the centerpiece.

MicroG Sentinel already demonstrates a useful loop: compare exercise evidence, find a gap, choose an eligible observation from an existing prescribed workout, then prepare a review. The current experience makes that loop difficult to see.

Preserve the engine and evidence discipline. Rebuild the hierarchy, episode flow and presentation around the next useful action.

Live inspection of the local prototype · Desktop 1280 × 720 · Narrow screen 390 × 844 · Eight audit steps · Thirteen captured screenshots · Product source files unchanged

Recommended overhaulScreenshot evidenceHackathon prioritiesScope and limits

The value proposition to protect

“MicroG Sentinel helps a crewmember understand changes in exercise response and choose the smallest useful follow-up observation from an already prescribed workout.”

The intended benefit is less collection and interpretation work. The prototype demonstrates a policy for choosing observations; it has not established real crew time savings, clinical accuracy or improved health outcomes. The differentiated interaction is the planner responding to changed evidence and workout availability.

The official health-monitoring challenge asks for gathering health indicators and helping astronauts evaluate and act on their health. Make that gather → understand → act sequence visible in the submission. NASA’s fitness-risk overview grounds the exercise and periodic assessment context; it does not validate this planner.

Six changes that would transform the demo

  1. Replace the long stacked page with a compact episode workspace. Use a compact source/participant/session header, an evidence comparison in the main area and the selected observation beside it. At a laptop viewport, the missing measurement, proposed observation and primary action should be visible together. Collapse the introductory hero into a useful episode title.
  2. Make replanning a visible interaction. Put the two prescribed workout opportunities next to the planner output. A user can mark one unavailable and immediately see the other selected, the changed modelled effort and a short explanation. Add a clearly labelled presenter mode for scenario variations; keep it separate from the crew task.
  3. Translate the engine’s states into human language. Replace IDs, ISO dates, “outside-baseline-range”, “insufficient” and “No eligible full cover” with useful titles, clear units and readable dates with a stated time zone. Preserve raw values in evidence details. Distinguish measurement change, evidence completeness and workflow state visually and semantically.
  4. Show evidence through useful graphics. For exercise, use paired baseline/current marks at each workload, with an explicit missing marker at 100 W. Label the baseline as two independent sessions; do not imply a normal population range. For NASA research, show actual occasion points for pre-test, post-bed-rest and recovery, with source and symptom context beside the chart.
  5. Make review preparation a readable outcome. Preview the packet in the interface before download. Show what changed, what supports the comparison, what remains unknown and the observation history. Label the result “Prepared locally”; expose JSON as an alternate export. A stale packet needs an obvious “Update review” action.
  6. Reduce navigation and finish the visual system. Primary destinations: Exercise episode, NASA evidence, About the prototype. Move formal VO₂ tools and the body map into supporting context. Use a consistent dark navy surface, clear off-white type, restrained teal actions, uniform inputs and explicit focus states. Use spacing and dividers before extra bordered cards. Replace the mobile comparison table with readable stacked workload rows.
Example first-screen copy · Synthetic demonstration

A heart-rate observation is missing at 100 W.

The earlier session cannot support a comparison at this workload. Two baseline sessions remain available.

Next useful observation: capture a new observation during the 100 W, 3-minute segment already included in the prescribed cycling session on 14 Nov at 09:00 UTC.

Why this opportunity: matching device and protocol context; covers the missing comparable observation; 1 modelled additional action.

Primary: Use this observation plan   Secondary: Prepare a review instead

Simulated crew data. The new observation remains separate from the original missing record. The added-action estimate is a demonstration assumption.

This example is derived from the actual synthetic fixture: DEMO-CYCLE, DEMO-PROTOCOL, 180-second stages and a 14 Nov 2026 09:00 UTC scheduled opportunity. It proposes clearer presentation of the existing plan, not a new workout or exercise prescription.

Alternative directions and trade-offs

DirectionWhat it emphasizesTrade-off
Episode workspace — recommendedEvidence, missing observation and adaptive selection visible together.Requires a meaningful layout and interaction pass, while retaining the existing logic.
Guided mission walkthroughA short sequence with presenter controls and a clear beginning and outcome.Strong for a recording; risks feeling scripted if it replaces the inspectable product. Use it as a demo layer.
Evidence-first research explorerNASA physiology, transparent calculations and source provenance.Good supporting evidence; makes the adaptive planner less prominent if used as the home screen.

Eight steps, with captured evidence

01

Open the exercise episode

Needs major redesign

The next-action concept and simulated-data label are useful foundations. At 1280 × 720, the exercise comparison is below the first viewport. A large heading, repeated setup copy, internal opportunity ID and ISO timestamp occupy the space where the user needs the actual missing measurement and workout context.

Change: Show “Heart-rate observation missing at 100 W” and the eligible prescribed cycling segment together. Keep the two independent baseline sessions and the missing-value state visible. Put IDs and raw timestamps in evidence details. Use the actual stage duration and device/protocol fields already in the data.

Accessibility / limits: The primary button is prominent; secondary controls look like unstyled white browser defaults. Exercise has no active-navigation indicator, confirmed by the DOM and App.tsx. A visible current section would improve orientation.

02

Change workout availability and observe replanning

Works; value is hidden

Disabling the first opportunity changed the selected opportunity from op-0 to op-1 and the modelled action count from 1 to 2. This is an actual recomputation. However, the controls are near the bottom and the result is near the top; the interaction requires scrolling between cause and effect.

Change: Give the demo a dedicated, clearly labelled scenario control beside the selected observation. Show the two available prescribed workouts as readable rows, the chosen row, its estimated added actions and why the other row was not chosen. Announce and highlight the changed selection in place.

Accessibility / limits: The visible checkbox itself measures 13 × 13 px, but it has an associated label; the effective hit area was not measured. Keep large clickable rows and verify keyboard focus and live announcements before claiming accessible interaction.

03

Accept a plan and collect a synthetic observation

Works; progress is unclear

Accepting the plan exposed “Generate synthetic observation”. Collection changed the comparison to a new synthetic session and removed the need for more collection. The page still uses the same generic heading and returns to the raw status “observed”; it does not visually explain that a new session now supplies the comparison.

Change: Show an episode history: original incomplete session → selected prescribed opportunity → new synthetic session → review preparation. Identify which observation the current values belong to. Preserve the original missing value. After collection, foreground “New observation available — review the change” rather than “No collection selected”.

Accessibility / limits: Use words and symbols as well as color for progress. A polite status region exists in the implementation, but screen-reader announcement behavior was not tested.

04

Prepare a review

Incomplete handoff experience

Review preparation correctly states that the packet is local and does not claim transmission. The interface reveals JSON/text downloads and a response box, but no readable on-screen packet. “Request review now” and “Prepare review” also split one intention across separate areas.

Change: Open a readable review preview containing the finding, current session, baseline sessions, comparison basis, missing evidence, observation history and source references. Make “Download review” the main action and JSON a secondary format. Put “Record a response” behind a separate disclosure. Show when the packet is stale and provide “Update review”.

Accessibility / limits: The textarea is labelled, which is a strength. A complete keyboard journey, validation handling and the downloaded file contents were outside this visual audit.

05

Inspect NASA exercise evidence

Credible content; weak presentation

The research view explicitly labels the bed-rest analog, laboratory context and recorded termination involving dizziness and breathing. The 100 W comparison is 166 bpm against two pre-tests of 124–125 bpm, a descriptive difference of +41.5 bpm. That useful story is spread across repeated text blocks, without a chart or baseline/post/recovery sequence.

Change: Use a separate “NASA evidence” view. At a selected workload, show the actual pre-test points, immediate post-bed-rest point and recovery point on a labelled occasion chart. Surface exertion and termination context beside it. Use a named selector such as “Immediately after bed rest · 6 May 2007”. Keep source rows and qualification available in an evidence drawer.

Accessibility / limits: Label individual points and provide a table equivalent. The observed two-session range is not a clinical threshold or confidence interval. Do not apply the crew planner to this research participant or treat the research as validation of prospective monitoring.

06

Explore Body Map and My Fitness

Competing product structure

The body map honestly labels four future modules, but they consume most of its panel. Its live link leads into the older VO₂ workflow rather than the exercise episode. My Fitness starts with an entry disclosure, then a long assessment explanation; its useful chart and follow-up are much farther down. The two research links in the main navigation also lead to different experiences.

Change: Make Exercise episode, NASA evidence and About the prototype the primary structure. Keep the body map as secondary context, with one useful active region and concise planned-module text. Place formal VO₂ assessments in supporting evidence with their own identity, source and units. Update the old submission/demo/usability documents to match the active exercise story.

Accessibility / limits: Status icons and text accompany the older colored badges, a strength to retain. Keep a text navigation alternative to the body graphic; do not rely on anatomical hot spots alone.

07

Exercise unresolved and direct-review states

Correct boundaries; unclear copy

No-opportunity leaves the missing HR explicit and offers review. Symptoms bypass collection optimization. These are valuable behaviors. They appear in nearly identical neutral panels with phrases such as “No eligible full cover” and “collection optimization bypassed”, making the different situations hard to recognize quickly.

Change: Use clear state-specific titles: “No matching workout is available” and “Review requested — no further collection planned”. State the missing evidence and explain the next available action. Keep the review path directly available. Do not imply emergency triage or a real message was sent.

Accessibility / limits: Give each state a text title and an appropriate symbol; never introduce a physiological red/green health classification. Verify focus and announcements when the scenario changes.

08

Read the episode on a narrow screen

Major readability failure

At 390 × 844, the header wraps into multiple rows, and the primary episode information still sits below setup copy. The comparison table compresses five columns until headings and values break across individual letters: Workload, Baseline HR, Difference and Unavailable become hard to read.

Change: Replace the narrow-screen table with one workload per stacked row: workload; baseline; current; difference; evidence status. Keep units attached to values and readable labels intact. Use compact navigation and place the next-action summary before secondary explanation.

Accessibility / limits: This is a directly observed readability problem. It is not, by itself, a complete WCAG conformance result. Test zoom/reflow, screen-reader table alternatives and the whole keyboard flow after implementation.

Build order for the hackathon

First: make one episode understandable

Rebuild the exercise first viewport; surface the missing 100 W observation; make planner alternatives and its explanation visible; translate internal labels; unify buttons and form controls; fix the narrow-screen comparison. Keep the existing computation, source isolation and saved episode behavior.

Next: show the complete outcome

Add the observation history and readable review preview. Make the synthetic collection transition visually explicit. Design the complete, unresolved, incompatible and direct-review states. Consolidate navigation and update the submission and usability scripts so they tell the current exercise story.

Then: strengthen the NASA evidence story

Build the occasion chart with the actual laboratory observations, source references, limitations and recorded termination context. Keep VO₂peak separate from exercise HR. Retain the body map as supporting context and polish its art only after the main flow is clear.

A concise judging demonstration

  1. Open on the gap: a synthetic cycling session lacks a comparable 100 W heart-rate observation.
  2. Show the decision: select the eligible prescribed opportunity that covers the gap with the fewest modelled added actions.
  3. Change the input: make that opportunity unavailable; the selection changes immediately, with an explanation.
  4. Complete the episode: collect a clearly labelled synthetic observation and preview the review packet. Preserve the original record.
  5. Ground it in NASA evidence: separately show the observed bed-rest response and source context. Explain that it illustrates the physiological measurement problem and does not establish prospective effectiveness.

Prepare a 30-second version of that story for a short submission asset, and a longer interactive version for questions. Verify the actual submission format in the official team form: the main submission guide could not be fetched during this audit, so this report does not certify its current requirements.

What makes the submission more convincing

Show the decision changing in response to a constraint, rather than narrating an algorithm the audience cannot see. Tie every claimed benefit to an observable behavior. A small, real usability exercise can check whether people identify the missing observation, understand the chosen opportunity, distinguish research from simulation and recognize that a local packet has not been sent. Report sample size, errors and time actually observed. Avoid a fabricated efficiency percentage.

Acceptance criteria for the redesign

  • A first-time viewer can identify the missing observation and next action without opening a disclosure.
  • At 1280 × 720, the key evidence and chosen opportunity are visible together.
  • Removing the selected opportunity changes the visible selection in place and explains why.
  • Collection visibly adds a new linked session; the historical missing value and frozen baseline remain intact.
  • No matching opportunity, incompatible evidence and symptoms each have a clear state and a direct review path.
  • A review is readable before export; a local preparation never appears as sent or received.
  • At 390 px width, units and labels remain readable without character-by-character wrapping.
  • Keyboard, zoom, screen-reader announcements and chart alternatives are checked in the implementation pass.

Scope, strengths and evidence limits

Preserve: the offline workflow; the distinction between simulated crew, NASA analog records and user transcriptions; explicit missing values and incompatibility; frozen baselines; the strict prospective comparison rules; minimal-action observation selection from existing prescribed workouts; symptoms bypassing collection; reproducible provenance; human-readable and structured exports.

Observed: the live exercise start, comparison, schedule availability change, plan acceptance, synthetic collection, review preparation, research view, body map, My Fitness, no-opportunity state, symptoms state and narrow-screen reflow. All thirteen screenshot files were captured and inspected in this audit run. Some are intentional full-page captures to preserve the surrounding context. Screenshot numbers identify captures; the numbered audit steps group related states.

Implementation inspected: App.tsx, index.css, Exercise.tsx, the synthetic scenario fixture and planner, plus the approved adaptive design and evaluation documents. These reads support specific findings about navigation, available metadata and modelled effort. This was not a calculation, security, regulatory or clinical audit.

Not checked: screen-reader output, complete keyboard journey, 200%/400% zoom, measured contrast across every state, real hardware, real transmission, export file contents, CSV import, fresh offline-disconnection testing, source-data re-curation, real users or clinical validity. No automated tests were run because no application code was changed. Clear labels, a skip link, semantic table headers, a status region and focus styles exist; they do not establish full accessibility compliance.

External grounding: the official challenge summary and NASA fitness-risk overview were checked. The 2026 event page reports submission closing on 15 November at 23:59 local time; confirm the team’s Local/Universal Event context and any earlier local judging deadline. The full current global judging guide and submission guide were unavailable through the research tool, so this report does not assign official scores or certify exact submission fields.

References: Official health-monitoring challenge · NASA reduced-fitness risk overview · 2026 event timeline. Physiological values in the screenshot findings describe the bundled prototype’s records; the original NASA download was not independently re-curated for this audit.
